correctness.rationale: For strongly monotone maximal monotone A,B with moduli μA,μB>0, H globally L-Lipschitz and θ∈[0,1], the first resolvent Q is firmly nonexpansive with Lipschitz q=(1+αμA)⁻¹. Expand ||(1+θ)z−θu||² using <z,u>≥||z||² to obtain sharp abstract transfer cθ²=θ²+(1−θ²)q²; skew resolvents attain this isolated transfer bound. The two-stage block estimate yields nonnegative Gθ; independently recomputed det(I−Gθ)=αβqs[μAμB−L((1−q)(1+θ)+cθ)] and Gθ≤G1. If μAμB>L, α sufficiently small (β arbitrary) makes G1 Schur and gives one positive-weight block-max norm contracting uniformly under EVERY switching sequence. Fixed-point equation independent of θ. Conversely scalar negative-feedback A=μAI,B=μBI,H=−LI has independently checked det(I−Tθ)=αβqs(μAμB−L), ruling out a universal strict contraction at ≤L at all steps, including equality. Claim is sharp class-level tunability, NOT fixed-step necessary criterion. Isolated transfer sharpness is not claimed for strongly monotone subclass.

originality.rationale: The algorithm and elementary firm-resolvent property are PREEXISTING. The October 2026 Qu–Wu–Chaffey available abstract/secondary mathematical account describes a coarser triangle-inequality certificate μAμB>L(1+2θ), not this common-weight, class-level tunability under switching. The refined Gθ matrix and scalar converse are explicitly different statements. Full primary paper was NOT accessible despite arXiv/OA attempts and authorized institutional download (VPN disconnected); no whole-document noncoverage finding is made, and this is a substantial residual priority risk. With available evidence, best-knowledge O is PASS, not certification.

This is material originality uncertainty, not an invented full-paper not-covering conclusion.
Sharpness of the isolated firm-resolvent bound uses merely monotone skew examples; it is not asserted within strong-monotonicity class. Rate optimization and fixed-step necessity remain open.
